communication_style.decision_format: Likes short comparison tables with total price, timing, key hotel amenities, and notable trade-offs rather than long narrative lists.
communication_style.follow_up_pattern: Often returns to verify hotel amenities, adjust return-flight timing after an agenda changes, or ask whether a slightly less convenient option is worth the savings.
communication_style.planning_voice: Concise and specific, usually giving origin, destination, dates, meeting windows, and reimbursement constraints up front.
communication_style.tone: Polite, direct, and collaborative; she appreciates caveats when a preference is soft or when availability is uncertain.

habit_interactions.description: For work hotels, included breakfast, an in-room coffee maker plus refrigerator or mini-fridge, and on-site or nearby restaurant access combine into a practical self-sufficiency pattern for early meetings and car-light arrivals.
On return days, she commonly wants the return leg after lunch so she can finish a morning site visit. United is favored from Chicago when comparable, but return timing can outrank carrier preference.
The queen-bed preference appears mostly as a quiet booking-detail check for standard one-bed rooms and should not override explicit separate-bed or multi-room arrangements.

habits.boundary_condition: Applies only as a non-exclusive airline preference; United is favored only among otherwise suitable options and may coexist with other acceptable preferred carriers.
habits.condition: When searching for commercial flights and no stronger current-trip carrier instruction overrides this preference.
habits.default_action: Give United positive ranking weight and include United among preferred carrier options when otherwise comparable, while still considering other suitable airlines.
habits.exception_condition: If United is unavailable, worse on primary itinerary constraints such as nonstop/timing/class, materially less attractive, or the user explicitly requests another carrier for the current trip, use or present the better alternative.
habits.name: soft_united_preferred_carrier
habits.preference_value: United is a soft preferred/acceptable airline, not an exclusive carrier requirement.
habits.scope_condition: Applies when Marisol is choosing commercial flights from Chicago for grant site visits, board meetings, conferences, or solo domestic trips where no stronger current carrier instruction overrides the choice.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat as a soft default; if true afternoon return departures are unavailable, limited, or unattractive, consider options close to afternoon.
habits.condition: When booking or comparing round-trip flights and selecting the return-leg departure time.
habits.default_action: Search for return-flight options departing in the afternoon and present those first when available.
habits.exception_condition: Do not apply as a universal outbound-leg rule; one supporting dialogue separately used a morning outbound while still preferring an afternoon return.
habits.name: afternoon_return_departure_preference
habits.preference_value: Prefer the return flight to depart in the afternoon.
habits.scope_condition: Applies to round-trip itineraries when she is choosing the return-leg departure after a work site visit, board meeting, conference, or short personal stay and does not have a fixed agenda or family constraint requiring another time.

habits.boundary_condition: Use this as a soft preference, not an absolute requirement, because the evidence ranges from a direct requirement to a tentative request and a later verification question.
habits.condition: When evaluating or booking a hotel, treat free breakfast as a recurring included-service preference.
habits.default_action: Prioritize or verify hotels with free breakfast when available; if breakfast is not listed, ask or check rather than assuming it is included.
habits.exception_condition: Do not reject an otherwise suitable hotel solely for lacking free breakfast unless the user explicitly makes it required in the current booking; do not infer a full or high-quality breakfast requirement unless stated.
habits.name: prefer_included_hotel_breakfast
habits.preference_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
habits.scope_condition: Applies when she is evaluating hotels for grant-site visits, conference stays, or personal overnights with early morning plans, especially when she is trying to keep the trip simple under reimbursement or per-diem rules.

habits.boundary_condition: Do not generalize this to other amenities such as microwave, balcony, bar, fireplace, room size, location, dates, or price.
habits.condition: When selecting or comparing hotel rooms and in-room amenities are being considered.
habits.default_action: Use an in-room coffee maker and refrigerator or mini-fridge as soft amenity criteria, and confirm availability when relevant.
habits.exception_condition: If a hotel otherwise strongly matches the current trip, treat a missing coffee maker or refrigerator/mini-fridge as a point to confirm with the user rather than an automatic rejection.
habits.name: hotel_room_coffee_maker_and_fridge_preference
habits.preference_value: Prefers a hotel room with both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
habits.scope_condition: Applies when she is comparing hotel rooms for multi-night work stays, conference hotels, or road-trip overnights where having practical in-room amenities would affect convenience.

habits.boundary_condition: Do not infer specific cuisine, star rating, bar service, kid-friendliness, downtown location, ski access, or wooded setting unless stated for the current trip.
habits.condition: When searching for, comparing, or summarizing hotel options.
habits.default_action: Mention on-site or nearby restaurant availability and use convenient dining access as a soft tie-breaker rather than a hard filter.
habits.exception_condition: Do not apply if the user explicitly deprioritizes dining access or if stronger current-trip constraints override it.
habits.name: hotel_restaurant_access
habits.preference_value: Hotels with on-site or nearby restaurant access, with restaurant availability noted during comparisons.
habits.scope_condition: Applies when she is searching for or comparing hotels on trips where she may arrive after a workday, skip a rental car, or need an easy dinner option near the hotel.

habits.boundary_condition: Evidence supports queen-size beds as the recurring preference. A king bed may be acceptable when explicitly offered or requested, but the evidence does not establish a reusable preference to upgrade to king whenever possible.
habits.condition: When booking a standard hotel room where a single larger/shared bed is appropriate and no separate-bed setup has been requested.
habits.default_action: Filter for or request a queen-size bed when bed type is selectable; if the listing only shows double, twin, or unspecified bedding, confirm the bed setup before booking.
habits.exception_condition: Honor explicit requests for twin beds, multiple separate beds, multiple rooms with different bedding, accessibility-related bedding, or any other trip-specific bed arrangement.
habits.name: queen_bed_for_single_bed_hotel_rooms
habits.preference_value: Prefer a queen-size bed for hotel rooms intended to have one larger/shared bed.
habits.scope_condition: Applies when she is booking a standard hotel room where one larger or shared bed is appropriate for a solo stay or a trip with her spouse, and no trip-specific separate-bed setup has been requested.

longitudinal_plan.travel_tempo: About ten to twelve travel episodes per year, heavier in spring and fall grant-review seasons, with a few conference or personal-weekend episodes filling the quieter months.
longitudinal_plan.typical_episode_shape: A normal episode spans two to four sessions: initial flight-and-hotel scan, refinement around meeting windows or reimbursement limits, hotel amenity verification, and occasional rebooking or receipt-style follow-up. Some conference trips collapse into one or two sessions because the dates and hotel block are fixed.

persona.decision_posture: Organized, reimbursement-aware, and practical. She cares more about low-friction schedules, predictable meals, and useful room amenities than luxury, and she will relax soft preferences when meeting times, hotel blocks, or budget rules are more important.
persona.name: Marisol Greene
persona.occupation: program officer for a national arts-and-culture grantmaking nonprofit
persona.travel_identity: Steady domestic traveler who self-books short grant-site visits to museums, libraries, and community arts organizations, plus board meetings, sector conferences, and a few low-key personal weekends each year.

travel_contexts.description: Solo two- to three-night trips from Chicago to visit grantee organizations, often with morning meetings, afternoon debriefs, and limited desire to rent a car unless the site requires it.
Domestic professional trips where the event hotel or a room block may constrain the hotel choice, but she still checks practical amenities before confirming.
Occasional short museum weekends or family visits with her spouse, sister, or adult daughter. Work habits soften, but her practical hotel preferences often still appear.
Weather disruptions, shifted site-visit agendas, and conference updates sometimes force rebooking; in those cases, explicit timing and availability constraints override recurring defaults.
